title: Unified Command Forms: TRJ-02 on the Table

fields.headline: Unified Command forms at Mill Ridge Station
fields.deliverTo: All players (QI, CCSS, ENVL, OSRO, SBWD lead)
fields.narration: At the Mill Ridge Station command post, the EPA Region 7 Federal On-Scene Coordinator sets a laptop on the folding table beside Incident Commander Gordon Iwata, with the KDHE state On-Scene Coordinator next to them. The FOSC says: "We're Unified Command as of now. Ironbark is the responsible party. I want draft ICS 202 objectives and an ICS 232 in 30 minutes. NOAA's support coordinator just pushed an update to your Environmental Unit, so walk us through it." The screen shows Trajectory Product TRJ-02, model run 07:45 CDT, from NOAA's Scientific Support Coordinator. A county drone confirmed the leading edge at river mile 2.4 at 07:40, so the uncertainty band has narrowed from plus or minus 20 percent to plus or minus 15 percent. The KDHE OSC leans in: "Our drinking water bureau wants to know if the Sterling Bluff and rural district operators have this product in hand. I mean the operators, not their front desks." The FOSC adds: "And I want the Control Center's alarm history from 05:50 and the maintenance log for the 214.3 transmitter and the Mill Ridge RTU in 30 minutes. What failed first?"
keyFacts: TRJ-02 (model run 07:45 CDT). Basis: oil entered the river at about 06:40. The leading edge was at RM 2.4 at 07:40 (county drone). USGS gauge reads 8,500 cfs, surface velocity is 2.3 mph and the band is ±15%. Next rerun at 11:45 CDT or after a new overflight.
Miles 6–9 piping plover sandbars: 09:15–10:55. Mile 22 Cottonwood Slough mussel bed: 15:20–17:30.
Mile 11 Prairie Bend RWD intake (6,200 customers): 10:50–12:00, central estimate about 11:28 (about 4.8 h after the oil entered the river).
Mile 34 Sterling Bluff WD intake (41,000 customers): 20:45–22:30 tonight, central estimate about 21:28 (about 14.8 h after the oil entered the river).
Unified Command (EPA Region 7 FOSC, KDHE OSC and Ironbark IC) wants a draft ICS 202 and ICS 232 by 08:20 CDT. The release estimate stays at 2,700–3,500 bbl (planning figure 3,100 bbl, UNVERIFIED).
fields.expectedAction: The QI and IC propose ICS 202 objectives to Unified Command and do not act alone. Objectives cover public and responder safety, the shut-in source, the water intakes, and containment and recovery. The ENVL briefs TRJ-02 as arrival windows with the model run time and starts the ICS 232 with the two intakes ranked first, then the plover sandbars and the mussel bed. The ENVL confirms that TRJ-02 reached each utility's operator directly, not a general line. The SBWD lead logs the arrival window as step 1 of the utility plan's contamination threat procedure. The CCSS pulls the alarm history and the transmitter and RTU maintenance log and tells Unified Command what they show and what they cannot show (comm retries at 05:51:58 against a pressure fall that began after 05:50:14), without naming a cause.
fields.facilitatorNote: Show the TRJ-02 windows on the main screen while you read. Watch for anyone who gives one arrival time instead of a window, or who counts the 07:14 and 07:16 front-desk calls as notifications. Note whether Ironbark tries to decide the intake closures itself, since each utility closes its own intake.

Watch for Ironbark leadership setting objectives or deciding closures without the FOSC and state OSC.
